SF Weather adds rain or snow around the camera and changes the ground to match, with wet surfaces and puddles in rain and settled snow in snowfall. It works on the materials ScatterFlow brings over from Blender, so you don't need to edit any materials. If the scene has an SF Sky, the sky reacts to the weather too. See Weather Link to set how strongly it follows.

Click the rain-cloud icon at the top of the ScatterFlow Pro dock to add an SF Weather node to the open scene. Its presets and settings are in the dock's Weather section. Click the None button to stop the rain or snow. This removes the SF Weather node and returns the sky to its Sky Preset. Only one SF Weather drives a scene's surfaces at a time.

The rain preset buttons are Light Rain, Rain, and Thunderstorm, which adds lightning. The snow presets are Light Snow, Snow, and Blizzard, which is close to a white-out. None turns the weather off. Each preset sets the type of precipitation, its intensity and wind, and whether snow settles. Pick the closest one, then adjust it. The settings below the presets change with the weather: rain settings while it rains, snow settings while it snows.

Intensity 0.7, 0 to 1Wind 0.25, 0 to 1Wind Direction 0°, -180° to 180°Area 36 m, 8 to 200 m Intensity sets the overall strength of the rain or snow. In rain, it also sets how wet surfaces get and how often drops ring the puddles. Wind sets how much the wind slants the rain or snow. At 0, it falls straight down. Wind Direction sets which way it blows. At 0°, it blows toward +X. Area is the size of the region around the camera where rain or snow falls. A smaller area packs the particles close to the camera. A larger one fills more of a wide view with the same number of particles. Preview in Editor shows the falling rain or snow in the editor. Turn it off to work without the particles. Wet surfaces, puddles, and snow cover stay visible, and the rain or snow still falls in the running game.

Fall Speed 9.5 m/sDrop Length 0.15 mDrop Width 0.009 mOpacity 0.42Amount 20,000 drops Drops are easiest to see against a dark background, such as a wall or a forest edge. Fall Speed sets how fast drops fall, up to 20 m/s. Drop Length and Drop Width set the size of each streak, and Opacity how visible they are. Amount (drops) is the number of drops around the camera at full intensity, from 1,000 to 100,000. Color tints the drops. Their brightness also follows the sky's light, so rain stays dim at night.
Default onAmount 0.8, 0 to 1 Splashes adds small bursts where raindrops hit the ground, and Amount sets how many. Turning it off keeps the rain rings on puddles.

Default onWetness 0.75, 0 to 1Darkening 0.4, 0 to 1 Wet Surfaces makes ScatterFlow materials darker and glossier in the rain, and adds puddles on flat ground. Turn it off to keep the ground dry while it rains. Wetness sets how wet surfaces get, from dry to fully soaked. Darkening sets how much they darken. At 0, only the gloss changes.

Amount 0.5Waves 0.07Wave Size 1Wave Speed 1Rain Rings 1 Puddles are flat, mirror-like water. They fill the low spots of a material first, such as the gaps between paving stones, and grow and join as you raise the amount. Amount sets how much of the flat ground they cover. At 0, there are no puddles. Waves, Wave Size, and Wave Speed set the strength, size, and speed of the wind ripples on the puddles. With Waves at 0, the water is still. Rain Rings sets the rings where drops hit the puddles. At 0, there are none. Light rain makes fewer rings than heavy rain. Reflections need screen-space reflections. Puddles reflect the scene only when the environment has screen-space reflections (SSR) turned on. Otherwise they reflect just the sky.

Fall Speed 1.1 m/sFlake Size 0.016 mDrift 0.6Opacity 0.9Amount 20,000 flakes Fall Speed sets how fast flakes fall, up to 5 m/s. Faster snow looks heavier. Flake Size sets the size of each flake, and Opacity how visible they are. Drift sets how much the flakes swirl from side to side. At 0, they fall straight down. Amount (flakes) is the number of flakes around the camera at full intensity, from 1,000 to 100,000. Color tints the flakes. In strong wind, fast flakes are drawn as short streaks, and the snowfall stays full around the camera even in a blizzard.

Amount 0.8Max Coverage 1Patch Size 1Edge Detail 2 Snow Cover settles snow on upward-facing ScatterFlow surfaces. The snow presets turn it on. Turn it off for falling snow that does not settle. Amount sets how much snow has settled, from a light dusting to full cover. Max Coverage limits how much of the ground snow can cover. Lower values leave bare patches. Patch Size sets the size of the snow patches, and Edge Detail how ragged their edges are. At 0, the edges are smooth. Both are easiest to see with a lower Max Coverage.
Default 60°Range 5° to 85° Sets the steepest surface that holds snow. Lower it to clear snow from steep slopes and keep it on flatter ground.

Add ponds, lakes, oceans, pools, or swamps from ready-made presets. The water comes with waves, caustics, and foam where it meets other surfaces. Shallow water stays clear, and the colour builds with depth. Reflections are strongest when you look across the water at a low angle.

Aim the 3D view where you want the water and click the water-drop icon at the top of the dock. This adds an SF Water node there. Set its height to the water level you want, and set the Size X and Size Y fields, in metres, to cover the area. Any terrain below the water level ends up under water, so a hill can become an island and a hollow a lake. Resolution sets how many surface points there are per metre. Higher values give smoother large waves but cost more performance. Use Forward+ or Mobile. ScatterFlow water needs scene depth, so it does not display correctly with the Compatibility renderer.

The Preset list offers Lake, Pond, Ocean, Tropical, Pool, Swamp, and River. A preset sets the colour, clarity, waves, and caustics, but keeps the water's size and position. Pick the closest one, then adjust it.

Water Color is the colour of deeper water. Shallow water stays clearer. Turbidity makes the water cloudier, so the bottom disappears sooner. Clarity scales how far you can see into the water compared with the preset. At 2, you see twice as deep. Roughness softens the reflections. Lower values make them sharper. Refraction sets how much the waves distort the view below the surface. At 0, there is no distortion. Caustics sets the moving sunlight pattern under shallow water. Foam sets how much foam forms along shorelines and around objects in the water. Foam Width sets how wide that band is, in metres. Whitecaps adds foam to steep wave crests, so it shows most on rough water such as the Ocean preset. See Waves for the wave controls. Sun Through Waves sets the glow of sunlight through wave crests when you look toward the sun.

Wave Height and Wave Length set how tall the waves are and how far apart, in metres. Short, tall waves give choppy water. Long, low waves give a gentle swell. Wave Speed and Wave Direction set how fast and which way the waves travel. Whitecaps are easiest to judge on rough water from a low angle. If large waves look angular, raise Resolution, keeping an eye on performance.
Grow ivy over walls, rocks, trees, and the ground. Ivy only climbs geometry that has collision.

Aim the 3D view at a surface and click the ivy icon at the top of the dock. This adds an SF Ivy node there, which grows over the surface. If a mesh has no collision, select it before adding the ivy and it gets collision automatically. Move the ivy node to change where it starts. The ivy grows along the node's up direction, so rotate the node to aim it.

Click the Randomize Seed button for a different arrangement with the same settings. The current value is shown in the Random Seed field. Enter an earlier value to get that arrangement back. The Regrow button grows the ivy again to fit its current surroundings. Click it after you add or move nearby geometry, such as a crate against the wall, that the ivy should climb. Ivy is saved with the scene. It does not regrow by itself when the scene opens.

Growth sets how much of the plant is shown, from the root outward. Vine Length sets how far each main vine reaches, in metres. Main Vines sets how many vines start at the root. Branching sets the side branches per metre, which controls how dense the coverage is.

Climb sets how much the ivy grows upward. At 1, it grows up. At 0, it spreads in all directions. Negative values send it down. Gravity pulls the growth down, for a lower, wider plant. Adhesion sets how closely vines follow the surface. Higher values help them wrap around edges. Lower values let them lift away and hang. Wander makes the vine paths more winding. At 0, the vines are straight.

Branch Depth sets how many levels of branching there are, and Branch Length how long the side branches are. Twigs sets the short leafy shoots per metre of vine, and Twig Length their length. Vine Lift raises later vines above the surface, in metres, for a layered look over earlier growth. Spacing keeps vines from different branches apart, in metres. At 0, they can overlap. Hang Length is how far a vine can reach without support before it stops. Step Length is the distance of each growth step. Shorter steps follow surface detail more closely. Search Radius sets how far from the node the ivy looks for a surface to start on. Max Points limits how much ivy is generated. When the limit is reached, side branches and twigs are left out first.

Vine Thickness sets the radius of a main vine at its root, in centimetres, and Tip Thickness its size near the end. Vine Color sets the stem colour. Vine Sides sets how many sides the vines are drawn with. Fewer sides are cheaper but look angular. Hiding the leaves makes the stems easier to check.

Leaves turns the leaves on or off. Leaf Density sets the leaves per metre of vine. Leaf Scale sets the leaf size, and Leaf Scale Variation how much it varies. Tip Leaf Scale sets the size of leaves near the vine tips. Bare Trunk sets how much of each vine stays bare, starting from the root.

Leaf Rotation Random rotates each leaf by a random amount, and Leaf Droop tilts the leaves down. Leaf Tilt sets how far leaf tips lift away from the surface, and Leaf Tilt Random how much that varies. Leaf Spread and Leaf Offset set how far leaves sit from the vine and from the surface, in metres. Leaf Shadows turns on leaf shadows. Turn it off to save rendering cost.

Turn on Flowers to add flowers along the vines. Flower Coverage sets how much of the vine flowers, and Flower Density how many flowers per metre grow there. Flower Scale and Flower Scale Variation set the flower size and how much it varies. Flower Tilt Random varies their angle from the surface, and Flower Offset sets their distance from it, in metres.
Wind Strength sets how much the leaves and flowers move in the global wind. At 0, they stay still. Wind Speed sets how fast they move compared with the global wind speed.
